rationale: The Latin anchors *odor*, *odoramen*, and the biblical phrase *odoratus est Dominus odorem suavitatis* ("the Lord smelled a sweet savour", Gen. 8:21) all point to a sensory exhalation — the air breathed out carrying a scent — which aligns with breath.n.02 ("the air that is inhaled and exhaled in respiration"), not the physiological process (breath.n.01) or a slight air movement (breath.n.05).
